properties.name: Vocabulary the schema declares can actually be written from the surface, and what cannot is reported rather than discovered one field at a time
properties.statement:
A property or edge type the schema declares must be writable through the tools a client actually has. Where it is not, the design should be able to SAY so — because the alternative is what happened four times in two days: a field that exists, is documented, is indexed for search, and that nothing can set.

THE FOUR INSTANCES, all found by hand, all inside one increment, and all the same shape:
1. `Verification.description` — declared, fulltext, the embedding field. Used ONCE in 164 Verifications, because `add_verification` had no parameter for it and `name` was the only string on offer. Read as "the team does not want descriptions"; it was unreachable, not unwanted.
2. `SUPERSEDES` — declared as an edge type with ZERO edges in the graph, while nine nodes named their successor in prose because no tool drew the edge.
3. `create_node`'s compare-and-swap — shipped with `expected_content_hash` as a required precondition and no `revision` block in the reply, so the value the tool demanded was unobtainable from the tool that demanded it. Every core test passed; the first MCP probe failed on line 1.
4. `GOVERNED_BY.ruling` — added to the schema and would have been reachable only through raw `create_edge`, caught before shipping only because instance 1 had happened hours earlier.

WHY THIS IS ONE FINDING AND NOT FOUR BUGS. Each was repaired at its own site, which is correct and is also how a pattern stays invisible. The common cause is structural: reflow2's schema and its typed constructors are written separately, nothing compares them, and the gap between "declared" and "writable" is exactly where a field goes to die. A corpus reading like "used once in 164" is then misread as a judgement about the team when it is a fact about the tools.

WHAT IS OWED. A computation over the schema and the served surface that answers: which declared properties and edge types can no tool set? `dec:idea-detect-vocabulary-that-nothing-reaches` already proposes something in this family and should be read before designing.

TWO THINGS IT MUST NOT DO, both of which would make it worse than nothing:
(a) It must not conclude that an unreachable field should be deleted. Three of the four above were WANTED and got a parameter; deletion would have been the wrong repair every time.
(b) It must not report raw `create_node` / `create_edge` as reachability. Those can write anything, which is precisely why they hid all four — a property is reachable when a TYPED tool can set it, and a finding computed against the generic escape hatch would answer clean forever.

RELATED AND DELIBERATELY DISTINCT: `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read` asks whether a distinction the schema draws is ever READ by a computation. This asks whether it can be WRITTEN at all. A field can fail either test independently.
